$comment: Golden wire vectors for the cross-SDK call envelope defined in
crates/flexiq-core/BINDING_CONTRACT.md: one tag byte (0x02 = CBOR) followed
by a CBOR-encoded [args, kwargs] pair.
Every SDK asserts this file in its own test suite, so a change to any one
runtime's encoding fails that runtime's build instead of silently producing
payloads its peers cannot read. Do not edit a hex string to make a test pass:
a diff here is a wire-format change and breaks every already-enqueued job.
For a client outside this repository, passing this file IS the conformance
bar — see contracts/REMOTE_SDK_CONTRACT.md, which ships in the same release
asset as these vectors and states the obligation each array carries.
`encode` cases pin bytes exactly. Every SDK must DECODE all of them; an SDK
must PRODUCE those bytes for every case its call API can express — see the
positional-only asymmetry below for the one exemption.
`decode_only` cases are the ones this file cannot state as an `encode` case,
for one of two distinct reasons:
- JSON cannot hold the value at all, so there is nothing to compare a
decode against and the bytes are the only thing left to pin. These carry
`round_trip_only` and DO assert bytes: 9007199254740993 loses a digit in
JSON, and a byte string has no JSON form.
- A conforming writer must not produce the bytes at all, and every reader
must still accept them. The two `float-narrow-*` cases are these: half
and single precision are widths the rules below forbid a writer to choose
and require a reader to read. Both are pinned, because a reader that
accepts one and refuses the other passes neither obligation.
`round_trip_only` asserting bytes is deliberate, not an oversight. Definite
length and shortest-form integers are contract rules, so there is exactly one
encoding of each of these values, and byte drift is the failure mode the
vectors exist to catch — the same class of bug as the indefinite-length
divergence, which interoperated fine and silently broke `auto:` keys.
One asymmetry is deliberate: a runtime whose call API is positional-only,
because its language has no keyword arguments, cannot PRODUCE a case with a
non-empty `kwargs` map. Every runtime must still DECODE those cases — a
worker has to run a job whose producer could express keyword arguments.
Three encoding rules make these bytes well-defined. Maps and arrays carry a
definite-length header — 0xa0 for an empty map, 0x80 for an empty array —
never the indefinite-length form (0xbf ... 0xff, 0x9f ... 0xff). Integers use
the shortest form that holds the value. A finite float goes the other way and
always takes the 64-bit head 0xfb, never 0xf9 or 0xfa, even where a narrower
width would round-trip the value exactly: 1.5 is fb3ff8000000000000, not
A NON-FINITE float is the stated exemption, and it is a library fact rather
than a choice. RFC 8949's preferred serialization spells an infinity or a NaN
in two bytes (f97c00, f97e00), and CBOR libraries hard-code that — some
without the option to write one wide, others without the option to write one
narrow — so no width is pinnable for either. A NaN's payload bits are free for
the same reason: a runtime's own NaN need not carry another's, and a writer
must not rewrite what it was handed. A payload carrying an infinity or a NaN
can therefore derive a different `auto:` key in each runtime; a caller that
needs deduplication sets `unique_key`. Neither is reachable through a
JSON-shaped producer at all — the gRPC `structured` door refuses both.
Every alternative those three rules forbid decodes to the same value, so a
runtime that picks one still interoperates — which is the danger. The
automatic `auto:` idempotency key hashes the serialized payload, so a
divergent encoder silently stops idempotent enqueues deduping across
languages. Readers must accept every form; writers must emit only these.

encode.name: no-args
encode.description: A call with neither positional nor keyword arguments.

encode.name: contract-vector
encode.description: f(1, 'a') — the vector pinned in BINDING_CONTRACT.md.

encode.name: kwargs-only
encode.description: Keyword arguments with no positional ones.

encode.name: positional-and-kwargs
encode.description: Both halves of the call body populated.

encode.name: single-object-arg
encode.description: One object as the single positional argument — the shape a task called from every SDK uses.

encode.name: negative-int
encode.description: Negative integers use CBOR major type 1.

encode.name: float
encode.description: A double takes the 64-bit head even though 1.5 fits half precision exactly.

decode_only.name: float-narrow-half
decode_only.description: The same 1.5 at half precision (f9 3e00) — a width a writer must not choose and a reader must accept.

decode_only.name: float-narrow-single
decode_only.description: The same 1.5 at single precision (fa 3fc00000). Pinned beside the half-precision case because a reader that takes one width and refuses the other satisfies neither obligation.

decode_only.name: int-beyond-double-precision
decode_only.description: 9007199254740993 — one past 2^53, where JSON would lose a digit. Value is not asserted because it is not representable in this file; decoding must round-trip to the same bytes.

decode_only.name: byte-string
decode_only.description: CBOR major type 2. Each runtime surfaces its own byte type, so only the round-trip is pinned.
